sentences.text: Agassizodus was a member of the class Chondrichthyes, a group of cartilaginous fishes.
It belonged to the family Helicoprionidae, which is sometimes called Agassizodontidae.
This predator featured a symphyseal tooth whorl at the tip of its lower jaw, paired with lateral crushing tooth plates.
The genus was named in 1875 based on tooth fragments and a massive jaw found in Osage County, Kansas.
It lived for over seventy million years, from 323.4 to 251.902 million years ago.
The type species Agassizodus variabilis was originally named Lophodus variabilis before that name was found to be preoccupied.
Some authors argue that the Eastman specimens and the Osage jaw represent an entirely new genus rather than Agassizodus or Campodus.
